questions.q: What is the key risk of an in-place upgrade compared to a side-by-side migration?
options: It replaces the existing instance directly, so there's no easy way back if something goes wrong
It requires a completely new server name and connection strings
It cannot be performed on production systems at all
It automatically raises every database's compatibility level
questions.explain: In-place upgrade overwrites the existing instance's binaries in place; side-by-side migration keeps the old instance running as a fallback.

questions.q: After an in-place upgrade, what happens to a database's compatibility level by default?
options: It stays at its pre-upgrade value; the new optimizer behavior is not activated automatically
It is automatically raised to match the new engine version
It is reset to the lowest supported level
Compatibility level is removed as a concept starting with SQL Server 2017
questions.explain: Compatibility level is a separate, per-database setting. Leaving it at the old value after an in-place upgrade is a deliberate, common practice to avoid immediate plan regressions.

questions.q: Why might a DBA deliberately delay raising compatibility level after an in-place upgrade?
options: A new compatibility level activates a new cardinality estimator and optimizer behavior that can cause plan regressions, so it's tested and raised as its own separate step
Raising compatibility level requires purchasing a separate license
Compatibility level cannot be changed without reinstalling SQL Server
Older compatibility levels run faster on all workloads, with no exceptions
questions.explain: The new engine's fixes are available immediately at the old compatibility level; the optimizer-behavior change is deferred until it's been tested deliberately.

questions.q: What does Microsoft's Data Migration Assistant (DMA) do, per this lesson?
options: Assesses a database for deprecated features and breaking changes before an upgrade or migration
Automatically performs the in-place upgrade with no DBA involvement
Replaces the need for backups before an upgrade
Only works when migrating to Azure, not for on-prem-to-on-prem assessments
questions.explain: DMA produces an assessment report of deprecated features, breaking changes, and behavior-change warnings, and is useful for on-prem-to-on-prem upgrades as well as Azure migrations.

questions.q: For a business-critical production system, which upgrade path does this lesson describe as the default choice?
options: Side-by-side migration, because the old instance stays available as a fallback
In-place upgrade, because it requires the least effort
Neither — major version upgrades should never be performed on production
Whichever path requires no downtime coordination
questions.explain: Side-by-side migration is the safer path for business-critical systems, even though it requires more coordination work, because the old instance remains as a fallback.
